claimBlocks.suggestedSection: A community’s own guidance on identity
claimBlocks.text: Wasagamack’s guide presents Anisininew as its preferred identity and rejects treating its people as simply part Cree and part Ojibwe. Its timeline recalls Island Lake statements in2018 and a wider naming announcement in February2024. The guide links language, shared history and self-determination. This is local community guidance, rather than permission to rename every northern Ontario nation or replace the spellings used by particular communities.

Butch Rabasto’s school account describes a transition from George Knott School to Wasagamack First Nation School during the2021–2022term. It places traditional learning, language and Elder guidance within education under the Wasagamack Education Authority. These are the school’s stated priorities and institutional history. They do not establish measured student outcomes, present enrolment or one educational program shared by every Anishininew community.

claimBlocks.suggestedSection: A distinct Garden Hill school context
claimBlocks.text: Garden Hill’s school describes secondary education through English with Anisinimowin and cultural learning integrated. It identifies families, Elders and Knowledge Keepers as partners. The short introduction helps readers locate a particular educational institution; its aspirations should not be mistaken for an independent evaluation or the same school system as Wasagamack’s.
